Subject: Intro: Clarence Mendez — availability for interview loop

Hi Sean / Ben / Marissa —

Hope you’re well. I’m Sophie from Tidebridge — I’m representing Clarence Mendez, a senior inference engineer with recent experience shipping production LLM inference services. Clarence is very interested in the Redwood Inference backend infra role and asked me to introduce him and share availability.

Quick context: Clarence is at a small startup now and has worked on serving runtime optimizations, quantization experiments, and cross-region deploys. He has an ML infra + backend background. I’ve attached his resume.

Candidate availability (PDT):
- Wed Jul 30: 9:00–11:30am or 3:00–5:00pm
- Thu Jul 31: 8:30–11:00am only

We’d like a 90-minute onsite-style loop (3 x 30-minute interviews) if that works — hiring manager + systems + ML infra. If you prefer shorter screens (2 x 45) we can adjust.

Please confirm:
1) which interviewers you’d like to include,
2) preferred windows (above), and
3) any prep or take-home that should be sent beforehand.

Attachments: clarence_mendez_resume.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Thanks —
Sophie Tilley

- Marissa Cole — ML Systems (30m) — model serving/quantization questions
- Ava Chen — Backend / Production (30m) — orchestration, observability, release policies

Candidate windows that work on our side: Wed Jul 30, 9:30–11:30am PDT (we could do 9:30/10:00/10:45 start times), or Thu Jul 31 9:00–10:30am PDT.

If Clarence can do the earlier Wed window that’s ideal. Otherwise Thu morning is fine. Please let me know which you prefer and I’ll send a calendar invite with the Zoom link.

Also — for the loop: no take-home is required up front; we’ll do live problem discussion and a short systems tradeoff scenario.

Subject: Re: Intro: Clarence Mendez — candidate feedback (quick debrief)

On Thu, Jul 31, 2025 at 1:30 PM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Perfect — I’ve scheduled the loop for Wed Jul 30 with a 9:30am PDT start (3 x 30m).

Quick notes from the interviews (short bullets):
- Overall: strong systems intuition; good tradeoff framing for KV-caching and prefix reuse.
- ML Systems (me): good grasp on quantization pitfalls, proposed a sensible approach (per-layer calibration + small eval set). Lacked depth on some sparse attention corner cases but salvageable.
- Backend (Ava): solid, clear on release rollback strategies and tracing. Implemented rate-limiting in prod before — relevant experience.
- Hiring manager (Ben): comfortable on architecture and team fit; asked for clearer examples of mentoring and incident ownership.

Recommendation: proceed to a short take-home (4–6 hour design + small code task) focused on KV cache warmup strategy and evaluation metrics. If he completes cleanly, move to final on-site loop.

Action items: Sean — can you confirm with Sophie that Clarence is willing to do the take-home and provide timeline (we typically give 5 business days)? Sophie — can you please relay and confirm candidate availability for the take-home window?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior ML Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
